newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to promote Hong Kong's autonomy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to promote Hong Kong's autonomy.

text.p: The United States will support Hong Kong's autonomy after it reverts to Chinese control on July 1, a senior U.S. official said on Thursday.

"U.S. policy toward Hong Kong is grounded in a determination to help preserve Hong Kong's prosperity and way of life," Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Jeffrey Bader said at a House of Representatives Asia Subcommittee hearing.
"In pursuing our commercial and law enforcement interests, we promote a framework of bilateral and multilateral agreements that support Hong Kong's autonomy from China.

"We intend to continue to grant Hong Kong a separate textile quota and maintain separate trade statistics for Hong Kong. We also plan to maintain a separate export control regime with Hong Kong, providing it preserves the same effective controls over sensitive technologies in the future as it does now," he said.

Bader said the United States would continue educational and cultural exchange programmes and would encourage high-level visits by U.S. officials and members of Congress to Hong Kong and U.S. visits by Hong Kong leaders.

He said Washington would be watching closely to see if China kept its word about continuing civil liberties and freedom of expression in Hong Kong. "We are deeply concerned about any effort to weaken these rights and freedoms in Hong Kong," he said.
Bader repeated U.S. objections to China's creation of a provisional legislature to replace the elected legislature and said he hoped elections would be held soon after July 1.

British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind also criticised China's action in an interview on Thursday with Reuters Television during a visit to Singapore, saying it violated the spirit of the 1984 Sino-British joint declaration.

Asia Subcommittee Chairman Doug Bereuter, a Nebraska Republican, introduced legislation on Thursday to give the president authority to modify U.S. laws affecting Hong Kong if China fails to allow a high degree of autonomy.

"Only if Hong Kong is permitted to retain this autonomy will it continue to be the prosperous, efficient, free and dynamic place that has made Hong Kong what it is today," Bereuter said. His bill would require the State Department to report on Chinese compliance with its agreements on Hong Kong.
